svg.text: Round 2 · knobs, bend/mod and faders · bought parts only · serves the full instrument and Little D
Owner: "finished instrument should be real parts" and, on bend/mod, "just getting creative here": wheels, sticks,
mini sticks, touch strips, faders, little dials. All laid out side by side below; nothing is decided. Every bend/mod
option is a pot underneath (eng v2 §2: mod is an analog pot), so each works electrically. Drawn at 1 mm = 7 px.
Checked against owner.md ("real parts"; "can we get creative with any of the knob / wheel styles"; bend/mod entries; silence) · eng v2 §2, §5 · budget-variant §3
1 · KNOBS (all bought; any colour; glow pointer = luminous paint on the bought cap)
Silence: all silent (no detents). Every MIDI-able knob gets the gold ring painted on the panel, not on the cap, so any cap style works.

Draw this round (bookbinding × "faced with a choice, do both"): one bought knob type, plus a strip of bookbinding leather on every rotating edge (knobs and wheels) = grip, silence, and it matches SLAB's sewn leather hinge.
2 · BEND AND MOD: the owner's lead, then every alternative side by side
LEAD · owner's pick: a one-way bend stick + a mod fader (or dial)
owner.md: joystick chosen; "joystick is great if we can go one direction"; bend springs back, mod stays put

g.text: dashed: full stick circle · slot: one axis

svg.text: Route 1: a true single-axis sprung stick (part UNVERIFIED).
Route 2 (sure to exist): a standard 2-axis thumbstick
(ALPS RKJXV-class) under a laser-cut slot in the panel:
the gate stops sideways travel; only Y is read.
Push = up, pull = down, let go = centre. Quiet springs.
≈ $3–10. Its pot sits in the MCU-read bend path (eng §2).
Mod: stays where you leave it
A short 20 mm slide pot + bought fader cap behind the
stick (drawn), or a small dial in the same spot.
Analog pot in the mod path, as eng v2 §2 requires.
≈ $1–2. Silent. Reads its own position: no light needed.
SLAB, MOTTO, DISH: the 13 mm zone at the left of
the keys (stick at the front, fader behind).
DOCK: the pod beside the panel.
Fit of the stick body (≈ 17 mm square) under a 13 mm
zone: UNVERIFIED; a mini stick is the fallback.
Drawn on every concept mock this round.
Bought thumbwheel pots, side by side
Fits the 13 mm zone, no width cost
Mod springs back: Y = mod while held
Bend X on one, mod Y on the other
Feel 3/5 · fingertip, like a tone switch
Feel 3/5 · bend from where you land
Above the keys or in the 13 mm zone
Bought 45 mm slide pot + fader cap
Mod stays put: perfect for mod
Mod: a plain small knob (stays put)
Mixes worth sampling (one hand each, no width cost unless noted)
Mini stick for bend + fader for mod: the lead above in a smaller part, if the thumbstick body doesn't fit the 13 mm zone.
Thumbwheel for bend + little dial for mod: the cheapest, smallest pair (Little D). · Touch strip for bend + fader for mod: no moving parts for bend at all.

Sprung sticks and mod: a sprung axis can't hold a mod depth. Either Y = mod only while held (Korg style), or pair the stick with a fader/dial for mod. A latching button would click: rejected (silence).
Electrical: every option above is a pot, so mod stays in the analog path (eng v2 §2). Hall-type mini sticks would need eng's E1 (mod as a VCA) first.
strip under the slot for dust
Bought wooden beads on 3 mm brass rods, each
coupled to a hidden slide pot · quiet with a
tick, ≈ $1.50–3) vs a pot with firmware

Retired (printed, so out per owner): printed knob caps (C1), printed wheels and edge wheels (C2, C3), printed abacus beads (C6), printed zipper rack for RANGE (C8). Edge wheels survive only with a bought thumbwheel pot.
Prices are rough catalogue figures (UNVERIFIED) except SoftPot $8.95 (eng budget-variant). The owner wants to see before buying: no quotes requested.
